v. dep., to arise, appear, spring up (class.): oboritur, nascitur, nam praepositionem ob pro ad, solitam poni, testis hic versus: tantum gaudium oboriri ex tumultu maximo, Paul. ex Müll.: tenebrae oboriuntur,: lacrimis ita fatur obortis,; : bellum,: laetitia,: vide, quanta lux liberalitatis et sapientiae mihi apud te dicenti oboriatur, * : sitis,: caligo, al.: verba, Oud.

la:verb:oboedio.gloss: to obey, yield obedience to (+dative of person obeyed)
senses: to obey, yield obedience to (+dative of person obeyed)
to be subject to, to serve
la:verb:oboedio.html:
ŏb-oedĭo (better than ŏb-ēdĭo, ; Mai.; ; cf.: oboedire, obaudire, Paul. ex Müll. and Bramb. s. v.— Ante-class. form of the
fut., oboedibo: oboedibo tibi, Afran. ap. ), īvi or ĭi, ītum, īre, 4, v. n.
ob-audio
.
In gen. (very rare), to give ear, hearken, listen to one: alicui,.—
Esp.
Prop., of living beings (class.).
To obey, yield obedience to. to be subject to, to serve (freq. and class.; cf.: pareo, obtempero, obsequor).—With dat.: parere, et oboedire praecepto,: legi,: voluntati,: obtemperare et oboedire magistratibus,: qui nobis oboediunt,: impulsu libidinum voluptatibus oboedientium,: pecora ventri oboedientia,: multorum oboedire tempori,.—Impers. pass.: utrimque enixe oboeditum dictatori est,.—
To be obedient in any thing (post-class.).—With acc. of neutr. pron.: atque haec omnia perfacile oboediebam,.— Absol., .—
Meton., of things, to yield, be manageable: ramus oleae quam maxime sequax, atque oboediturus,yielding, flexible,.— Hence, ŏboedĭens (ŏbēd-), entis, P. a.
Prop., of living beings, obedient, compliant (freq. and class.).
With dat.: nulli est naturae oboediens aut subjectus deus,: natio semper oboediens huic imperio,: appetitum rationi oboedientem praebere,: vivere oboedientem alicui,.—Comp.: imperiis nemo oboedientior,.—Sup.: imperiis oboedientissimus miles,.—
With ad: ad nova consilia gentem oboedientem habere,.—Particular phrases.
Dicto oboedientem esse alicui for dicto audientem esse alicui, to be obedient to one's word or command: magistro desinebat esse dicto oboediens,; cf.: nec plebs nobis dicto audiens atque oboediens sit,. —
Omnia secunda et oboedientia sunt, according to your wishes, .—
Absol.: cujus vis omnis in consensu oboedientium esset,the obedient,.—
Transf., of things, yielding, manageable: oboedientissima quocumque in opere fraxinus,i. e. easily wrought,.—Hence, adv.: ŏboedĭ-enter, obediently, willingly, readily (a favorite word of Livy; elsewh. very rare): conferre tributum, : facere imperata,: facere adversus aliquem,.—Comp.: nihil oboedientius fecerunt, quam, etc.,.—Sup.: oboedientissime paruit, , 22, 8.

la:noun:oboedientia.html:
ŏboedĭentĭa (obed-), ae, f.
oboediens
,
obedience (class.).
Of persons.
With gen.: servitus est oboedientia fracti animi,.—
Absol.: relinquunt enim et abiciunt oboedientiam,. 102.—
Of bees: mira plebi circa regem oboedientia,.—
Of elephants: intellectus illis sermonis patrii et imperiorum oboedientia,.

la:noun:obolus.html:
ŏbŏlus, i, m., = ὀβολός.
Lit., an obol, a small Greek coin, the sixth part of a drachm, equivalent to three and a half cents Federal currency, : siclus viginti obolos habet,.—
Transf., as a weight, the sixth part of a drachm Fann. de Ponder. et Mens. 37; cf. ; ; : trium obolorum pondere,.
